A_target.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite [[Definition:Graph (Graph Theory)|graph]] with $m$ edges.
Then $G$ has a [[Definition:Bipartite Graph|bipartite]] [[Definition:Subgraph|subgraph]] with at least $\dfrac m 2$ edges.

B_source.statement:
Let $X$ be a [[Definition:Random Variable|random variable]] on a finite [[Definition:Probability Space|probability space]] with $\expect X \ge c$.
Then $X \ge c$ for at least one outcome; so to show that an object with $X \ge c$ exists, it suffices to compute an expectation.

substitutions.the random object: a uniformly random vertex subset S
substitutions.the random variable X: the number of edges crossing between S and its complement

derived.an outcome with X >= m/2: a cut with at least half the edges

object_map.reformulation: Apply the probabilistic method in its expectation form to a random bipartition.

validity_conditions: Linearity of expectation needs no independence between edges.
The argument derandomizes by the method of conditional expectations.
proof_plan: Put each vertex into $S$ independently with probability $\dfrac 1 2$.

An edge crosses between $S$ and its complement with probability $\dfrac 1 2$.
By [[Expectation is Linear|linearity of expectation]], the number $X$ of crossing edges has $\expect X = \dfrac m 2$.
By the source result, some choice of $S$ has $X \ge \dfrac m 2$.

The crossing edges form a bipartite subgraph with parts $S$ and $V \setminus S$.
{{qed}}
